_about: FOUNDER-APPROVED public wording for the Borrowed Garden Provider Explorer (evidence pack approved 13 Oct 2026, with conditions). Every sentence names its Atlas sources and whether it is time-sensitive. Edit only with founder approval. The unconfirmed Community Roots referee requirement is deliberately absent (founder ruling 13 Oct 2026).

tabs.label: Garden-sharing services
tabs.note: Services that introduce garden owners to people who want to grow.

tabs.label: Other growing opportunities
tabs.note: Council-run allotments. These are not garden-sharing services: they are council plots with their own waiting lists.

ORG-000202.subtitle: Soil Mates garden-share programme

offers.t: A garden-share programme, Soil Mates, that pairs people who have a garden with people nearby who want to grow food.
Each pairing receives a raised bed, compost, seeds and an online growing course.

where.t: Dublin, where it has made pairings since 2022, with a programme in the Liberties, Dublin 8.
Six local projects have been started through ChangeX, including Rush, Co. Dublin.

how.t: A local volunteer coordinator matches garden owners with growers and introduces them at a pairing meeting.

ORG-000202.relationship: PlotNua has no relationship with Community Roots.

ORG-000203.subtitle: Online matching service, free to join

offers.t: A free online service where people looking for growing space and people with spare garden or land register separately.

where.t: Starting in Irish cities, suburbs and nearby towns.

how.t: Exact addresses stay private and contact details are shared only when both people say yes; any arrangement is then made directly between them.
On its own published figures it has 78 grower requests, 3 offers of space and no matches so far, and the insurance it hopes to arrange is not yet in place.

ORG-000203.relationship: Early and unproven. PlotNua has no relationship with Homegrown.ie.

ORG-000204.subtitle: Allotments and community gardens

offers.t: Council-run allotments and community gardens at nine sites. This is not garden-sharing.

where.t: Dublin city. Most of the listed sites are in Dublin 8 and Dublin 12.

how.t: You email the site you want and join its waiting list; licences are assigned as plots become free.
The council says all available allotments are currently assigned.

ORG-000204.relationship: PlotNua has no relationship with Dublin City Council.

ORG-000205.subtitle: Allotments

offers.t: About 900 council allotments across four sites: Balbriggan, Skerries, Turvey and Powerstown. This is not garden-sharing.

where.t: Fingal. Only Fingal residents can apply, with one plot per household.

how.t: Applications open once a year, in January, and each site's waiting list is capped at 50.
For 2026 Powerstown and Turvey took no new applications because their lists were full.

ORG-000205.relationship: PlotNua has no relationship with Fingal County Council.

ORG-000206.subtitle: Allotments

offers.t: Council allotments at two sites: Goatstown (136 plots) and Shankill (95 plots). This is not garden-sharing.

where.t: Dún Laoghaire-Rathdown. Residents only, one plot per person.

how.t: Plots are allocated first come, first served from a waiting list.
The council is not currently accepting applications because both waiting lists are extensive (its notice is dated September 2024).

ORG-000206.relationship: PlotNua has no relationship with Dún Laoghaire-Rathdown County Council.
